answer: Physical Kernel Attestation. Each identity is bound to a measured boot kernel whose signing key is sealed in a TPM on a single physical device, and the registry admits one kernel hash per silicon die. A knoll of attested dies reports their own hashes; duplicates are pruned on sight. Faking an identity requires fabricating a die with a unique onyx-marked ROM and defeating remote attestation, so each admitted identity costs one whole physically distinct device, not a software copy.
